decisive_items: Chronic hypomagnesemia requiring parenteral magnesium sulfate through a mediport twice weekly
Initial blood cultures: positive for Gram-positive rods
Mediport cultures: positive for Gram-positive rods after three days
response.rationale: Fever and chills in a patient with an indwelling mediport plus concordant blood and mediport cultures growing Gram-positive rods indicate catheter-related bloodstream infection. Normal urinalysis and chest radiograph reduce UTI and endocarditis, and Bacillus species is not explicitly confirmed by the vignette.

rejected.why: Too nonspecific; patient was afebrile with normal lactate and no organ dysfunction.
Only historical; no acute post-nephrectomy complication is evidenced.
Chronic baseline condition, not the acute febrile presentation.
Same as chronic hypomagnesemia; not the acute diagnosis.
Bacillus species is not explicitly identified; Gram-positive rods and CDC sequencing do not confirm the genus.
No cardiac or embolic findings; Gram-positive rods and mediport cultures favor line infection.
Bacillus species is not confirmed and the catheter-related context is better captured by R10.
